content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: model-family 'cobalt13b' sustained RPM spike detected. Queue buildup and increased 5xx/429 observed across us-west-2 and eu-central-1. Link: https://monitoring/redwood/alerts/2069012345

alice: seeing same. tail p95 token latency climbing. most requests are short-chat workloads.

jamie: 429s from rate-limiter at ingress layer. Appears per-family rate policy got bypassed for some old clients after yesterday's rollout.

morgan: confirmed affected customers: AcmeCorp (prod), NovaPay (staging but high traffic), and internal smoke tests. AcmeCorp has ~18% error rate on cobalt13b calls.

lee: quick ask — do we want to throttle the family or disable cobalt13b entirely until we roll a fix?

alice: prefer surgical approach. lower RPM/TPM for cobalt13b per-region, enable fallback to cobalt13b-quant (quantized variant) and route non-critical routes to smaller model.

ananya: I'll own the quota change. prepping commands.
ananya: Applying per-family RPM cap in control plane now. command:
```bash
curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/v1/quotas/update \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTL_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"family":"cobalt13b","region":"*","rpm":200,"tpm":12000, "note":"temp relief - 2069012345"}'
```

ananya: Pushed change at control-plane. waiting for propagation (~30s).

devops-bot: quota update accepted. id=qt-8c4b, target propagation 45s.

jamie: seeing immediate reduction in 429s at the ingress. p95 token latency starting to decline.

morgan: reached out to AcmeCorp SRE lead (Ben). Ben reports degraded UX but stable errors down from 18% -> 6%. He asked if we can allow burst for their auth route.

alice: we can create an exception for AcmeCorp auth route if they provide exact route id. prefer to avoid customer-specific exceptions unless necessary.

lee: enabling automatic fallback to cobalt13b-quant for existing sessions that exceed rpm cap. patching routing policy: if rpm_exceeded -> route to quant variant or to cobalt13b-lite.

alice: please add rollout note and timeboxed policy (30m).

ananya: added fallback rule via routing API:
```json
{"when":"quota_exceeded","action":"route_family","from":"cobalt13b","to":"cobalt13b-quant","ttl":"30m","created_by":"ananya","ticket":"INC-2069012345"}
```
(note: above is payload sent, control-plane accepted).

devops-bot: routing rule applied. rid=rt-91f2.

jamie: metrics now show core latency p95 down 28% vs peak. throughput normalized. Error budget improving.

morgan: customer update: Ben says they can tolerate the throttle for 30m. he appreciated quick response.

alice: next steps: 1) root-cause triage — confirm rollout change yesterday that allowed bypass; 2) plan revert/fix; 3) coordinate oncall handoff in 30m if still unstable.

ananya: tagging eng-sre for deeper investigation. @eng-sre please pick up RCA for control-plane rate policy.

lee: I'll prepare a short post-incident note and capture timelines + commands executed.

jamie: creating a short runbook snippet to undo the quota if we need to reopen capacity:
```bash
# remove temporary rpm cap
curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/v1/quotas/remove \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTL_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"family":"cobalt13b","note":"removal temp cap"}'
```

alice: handoff in 30m to @morgan (night shift). current status: mitigated via per-family RPM cap + fallback routing. customer impact reduced but not zero. continuing root-cause.

morgan: noted. I'll watch for propagation and customer escalations. if error rate <2% and latency stable for 15m, will close incident channel.

ananya: logging final snapshot of quotas and routing decisions to INC ticket.

devops-bot: snapshot saved id=snap-2069012345.

alice: thanks everyone. escalate to eng-sre for postmortem.

# end of thread
